full_judgment:
5. Leave was granted to consider whether the judgment of the lower appellate Court was a proper judgment of reversal in view of the unchallenged assertion of P.W.1 (Plaintiff No. 3) that Jogesh Chandra Shaha went to India in 1971 during the war of liberation and not during the Indo-Pak war of 1965 as stated by the Government and that the finding that Jogesh Chandra was in exclusive possession of the suit land is contrary to the record of right Ext. 1 (b). 

 6. On the pleadings of the parties, the material question for determination was whether the property could be lawfully treated as a vested and non-resident property. If it is found that Jogesh Chandra Shaha left for India before the Indo-Pak War 1965 then his 1.95 acres of land in Plot No. 1413 could be taken over as a non-resident and vested property. But, if it is found that Jogesh Chandra left for India in 1971, then whole complexion of the case will be changed, and the suit property cannot be treated as a non-resident and vested property. To determine this material issue, the evidence of P.W.1 who is plaintiff No. 3 in the suit and full brother of plaintiffs Nos. 1 and 2 is very material. In his deposition, he categorically stated that Jogesh Chandra went to India during the war of liberation in 1971 and it was not a fact that Jogesh Chandra left the country before 1965 Indo-Pak War. This witness further stated that the R.O.R. Ext. 1 (b) was prepared and published not in the name of Jogesh Chandra alone but in the name of Jogesh Chandra showing 1/3rd share along with 1/3rd share of his father and that there was no partition of the property by metes and bounds. This R.O.R. Khatian also shows share of Jogesh Chandra and others. D.W.1 Zahurul Huq, tashilder of Vested Property Section under Kasba Police Station submitted from his report that there was no mention that Jogesh left for India in 1965, that the Government took over possession of the suit land and that there was no order passed by the S.D.O. to deliver possession to the lessee. This being the nature of evidence, the trial Court was correct in holding that the vested property case that was started in 1980-81 had no basis whatsoever. Further, the trial Court considered another aspect that plaintiff No. 2, son of Golak Behar, executed Kabala Exhibit 3 on 4.2.89 in favour of defendants Nos. 4-9. This fact is also admitted by P.W.1 and P.W.3 Arab Ali. Hence, the trial Court believed that Golak Behari got the suit property by an amicable partition. The lower appellate Court did not consider this material aspect as to the fact that Jogesh Chandra left for India in 1971 during the war of liberation. Nos. consideration of this material evidence of the plaintiff by the lower appellate Court and consequently treating the property as non-resident and vested property without any evidence on record, either oral or documentary, had vitiated the judgment of the lower appellate Court. Hence, the judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal. Mr. Moksudur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the Assistant Custodian, Vested and Non-resident property, also finds it very difficult to support the judgment of the high court Division. Thus, the impugned order of the learned single Judge of the High Court Division summarily rejecting the revisional application is set aside and the judgment of the trial Court is restored and the suit is decreed.
